answer: A sybil tax charges each identity a sunk fee that is never refunded. Like light through a prism, one budget splits across many copies, yet every copy pays in full: joining costs 10 days of expected earnings. Raising 100 identities costs 1,000 days upfront, piling like sand into a dune, and a canyon of checks leaves each copy taxed again. Honest agents pay once and keep undiluted rewards, so bulk forgery costs more than it earns.
